newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus expels U.S. diplomat after anti-govt demo.
newsitem.headline: Belarus expels U.S. diplomat after anti-govt demo.

text.p: Belarussian state television said on Sunday that a U.S. diplomat had been asked to leave the former Soviet republic after taking part in an anti-government rally.

News anchorman Alexander Zimovsky read out a Foreign Ministry statement saying the embassy's first secretary Serzh Alexandrov, an ethnic Belarussian, had taken part in actions "incompatible with his diplomatic status".

"In connection with the fact that his activities were incompatible with his diplomatic status...he has been declared persona non grata and has been asked to leave the borders of the republic of Belarus," Zimovsky said.

The statement said Alexandrov had been detained earlier on Sunday for "provocative actions" during violent clashes between riot police and nationalist demonstrators protesting against the pro-Moscow policies of hardline President Alexander Lukashenko.

It added that he had been released as soon as his diplomatic identity had been established. About 70 other people were arrested, including two prominent liberal politicians, who were also later released.
Before reading the ministry statement, Zimovsky said foreign intelligence organs had been involved in the nationalists' rally and said Alexandrov had been working as a spy.
He added that the U.S. embassy, in violation of all diplomatic norms, had been putting "crude pressure" on the country's interior ministry in recent days but gave no further details.
There was no immediate reaction from the embassy to news of the expulsion.

Earlier the embassy's official spokeswoman, Janet Demery, said Western diplomats often watched Belarus protests from the sidelines "as part of a brief to observe the political situation but not to participate."

The United States has become a vociferous critic of Lukashenko's increasingly authoritarian rule and recently announced it was cutting off $40 million in aid to the country of 10 million because of its human rights performance.

Sunday's rally was the latest in a string of protests against Lukashenko, who has cracked down on opposition forces by restricting rallies, arresting protesters and putting a senior opposition leader in prison in recent weeks.
The nationalists also object strongly to Lukashenko's building closer ties with Moscow, though most people in the small, land-locked republic support this policy.
The protesters hurled chunks of ice, smashed police car windows and yelled "Long live Belarus!". Police used truncheons and teargas to quell the protests.
